newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures cut gains, finish higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures cut gains, finish higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures cut their biggest gains during the final 90 minutes but still finished fairly busy pit trading moderately higher.
Futures, which erased early losses and shot higher at midmorning with U.S. Treasury bond futures, followed T-bond futures down from their peaks before wandering in a range.

T-bond futures shook off early weakness caused by strong economic growth and rose partly on supply-related factors, including official comments suggesting a U.S. budget deal could come soon and talk that the U.S. Treasury could decide to curtail some auctions of 10-year notes.

Before midday, U.S. Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said he believed budget negotiators were "very close" to reaching an agreement with the White House and that he was still "hopeful" an agreement could be reached Wednesday.
Later, Treasury announced it would sell $29 billion of securities next week.

It also said that in light of the Treasury's expected paydown of $65 billion in debt in the second quarter, linked to a surge in tax receipts, it would consider a private-sector committee's recommendation to drop two of the six auctions of 10-year notes it holds annually. No decision has been made yet.
Brokers tied part of the day's strongest rally to signs of month-end portfolio adjustments as shorts bailed out and fresh buyers appeared.
They also cited a softening of the rate-hike fears that had smacked futures sharply lower near the outset following report of a much stronger than expected performance by the economy last quarter.

T-bond futures retreated, dragging down S&P 500s futures in electronic trading, after first-quarter U.S. gross domestic product surged 5.6 percent. But some later said the buildup of business inventories softened the impact of the GDP rise.
Futures moved little when April's Chicago purchasing managers index slipped to 57.2 from 57.5 and against forecasts for 56.2. Prices fell to 53.3, and employment rose to 56.1.

Technically, some chartists said the outlook turned more skewed to the upside even though futures appear overbought and backed off from their 810.00 peak. Some brokers also questioned the durability of the rally fundamentally.
"Above 806, it was a crazy, bizarre-o day," said one skeptical floor broker. "They've got the shorts in a vise."
"Today, I think we just basically guaranteed they (Fed) are going to hike rates," said another broker of GDP rise.

"The tech stocks are all fired up about strong growth and are not so worried about it (Fed) stomping on the brake," the second broker said. "But I'm leery of it.... What if the Fed surprises us with a 50-basis-point hike?"

June S&P 500s hit buy stops several times during the rise, which also drew arb buy programs until the Dow 30 average rose 50 points and triggered the New York Stock Exchange's curb on computer-assisted index arb.

June S&P 500s rose 3.00 to 802.80, Value Line lost 0.30 to 700.20, Midcap lost 0.35 to 257.35, Nasdaq up 13.60 at 879.35, Russell up 0.65 to 344.90, Nikkei rose 565.0 to 19,440.0. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
